svg.text: Object lifecycle across the ext boundary — four disciplines, only one of them safe by construction
Green = library protects the object against a client release racing an in-flight frame. Red = the client carries the obligation.
CLIENT — Chromium VEA
LIBRARY — NVPRO encoder session
1 · Input images — registered, refcounted, deferred release ✔ SAFE
Client allocates the dma-buf (Ozone pixmap) and exports an fd.
Ownership TRANSFER: the fd is consumed on every exit path,
including failure. The client must not close it afterwards.
RegisterImageResource(desc, &resourceId)
resourceId — generation-counted
Library allocates the VkImage, VkDeviceMemory and view.
Registration is refcounted for the lifetime of each submitted frame.
UnregisterImageResource defers while frames are in flight —
it never frees memory the GPU is still reading.
Stale id → ERROR_RESOURCE_UNKNOWN, never a recycled-slot match.
2 · Registered semaphores — same id shape, opposite lifetime guarantee ✘ CLIENT'S BURDEN
Client creates the timeline semaphore and exports an OS handle.
On Windows the client must DuplicateHandle on the importing side
and close its duplicate once registration returns.
RegisterSemaphore(desc, osHandle, &resourceId)
UnregisterSemaphore does NOT defer. The imported VkSemaphore is
destroyed before the call returns.
The client must prove every batch that waits on or signals it has
completed (VUID-vkDestroySemaphore-semaphore-01137) first.
Never-retired registrations are safe: destroyed at teardown, queue idle.
3 · Raw semaphores in VkVideoEncoderFrameSubmitInfo — no id, no refcount, no defer ✘ UNTRACKED
pWaitSemaphores / pSignalSemaphores are raw VkSemaphore arrays.
The header is explicit: "the caller's semaphores belong to its own
SubmitRegisteredFrame(info with raw handles)
The library stores the handles into a submit batch and returns.
Nothing records that the batch depends on them. Destroy one while
the batch is pending and the failure is a driver-level use-after-free.
4 · Per-frame fences — fd ownership, and it flows BOTH ways ◑ EXPLICIT, ASYMMETRIC
acquireFenceFd (in): the library consumes it on every exit —
including RESOURCE_LIMIT refusals, which import before they count.
VkVideoEncoderFrameFenceDescriptor
*pReleaseFenceFd — the CLIENT now owns this fd
pReleaseFenceFd (out): the exported fd is the caller's. The library
never closes it — close(2) it, or hand it to exactly one import.
−1 means "no fence", NOT failure, and never means "input already released".
What Chromium actually does — the two hazards are latent in the API, not live in this embedder
• Sets pWaitSemaphores = pSignalSemaphores = nullptr. Discipline 3 is never exercised; per-frame sync rides the fd fences instead.
• Never calls UnregisterSemaphore. Registrations live to session teardown, where the queue is already idle — so discipline 2's
obligation is discharged by never invoking it, not by proving it safe.
Both are avoidance, not protection. Another embedder using the documented API as written reaches both hazards immediately.
